title: Level Up Your Phone Agent
summary: Teach your phone agent to do real things: book your calendar, log calls to a sheet, post to Slack, or reach apps Vapi doesn’t have, like Spotify and Notion, through n8n. Three self-paced stations, from your very first agent to custom workflows.
detail: Three stations, at your own pace, headphones on. Station 1 is for anyone without a phone agent yet: build one in about 20 minutes with Deepgram Flux, Claude Haiku and a free Vapi number. Station 2 uses Vapi Composer, a chat box that builds for you, and Vapi's built-in tools: Google Calendar, Google Sheets, Slack, transfers and more. Station 3 connects your agent to n8n for the apps Vapi doesn’t have built in, like adding a song to a Spotify playlist or saving an idea to Notion. Show and tell at the end.
outcome: A phone agent with at least one working tool, so a phone call makes something real happen.
prereqs: A laptop with Chrome, headphones with a mic, and your phone.
Came to Build Your First Phone Agent? Bring your Vapi login. Your agent is ready for station 2.
New? Nothing to set up in advance; station 1 covers it.
For tools: a Google or Slack account you don't mind filling with test data.
Station 3: a free n8n account (14-day trial, no credit card).
artifact: A live phone agent that books, logs or posts something real when you call it.

slides.title: Everything you can do in Vapi
bullets: Composer: describe what you want in plain English and it builds it
Tools: API Request, Function, Transfer Call, Hang Up, Send Text, Dial Keypad, Handoff, Voicemail, Query, MCP
Built-in apps: Google Calendar (check and book), Google Sheets (add a row), Slack (send a message), GoHighLevel (contacts and calendar)
Zapier, Make and Composio plug in as MCP servers
Knowledge base: upload your files and the agent answers from them
Squads: a team of assistants that pass the call to each other
Phone numbers: a free US number for incoming calls, or bring Twilio, Telnyx or Vonage to call out
Campaigns: call a whole contact list, with voicemail detection
Structured Outputs and call analysis: name, order, mood and a summary from every call
Evals and Simulations: an AI caller tests your agent before real people do
Call logs, recordings, transcripts, Boards and alerts
Text too: chat assistants, inbound SMS and a widget for your website
slides.note: VITALI'S SLIDE: hand the mic to Vitali from Vapi to present this one. Don't read it all. This is the menu: point at two or three things people get excited about (Composer, Google Calendar, Squads, Simulations). Pattern for any tool: Integrations to connect Google or Slack, Tools then Create Tool, attach it on your assistant's Tools tab, Publish. Or just ask Composer. Vapi Workflows were retired in August, so don't send anyone looking for them.

slides.title: Everything you can do with n8n
bullets: 2,000+ apps you connect by dragging boxes on a canvas
Sales: HubSpot, Salesforce
Messages: Slack, Discord, Telegram, WhatsApp, Twilio texts
Data: Notion, Airtable, Google Sheets, Postgres, Supabase
Stores and payments: Shopify, Stripe
Email and calendar: Gmail, Outlook, Google Calendar
Files and code: Google Drive, Dropbox, GitHub
Fun: Spotify, Philips Hue, Home Assistant
AI Agent node with Claude, memory and your own documents
Logic: If, Switch, loops, Wait, schedules, and your own JavaScript or Python
Deepgram, Vapi and anything else with an API: the HTTP Request node
Free n8n Cloud trial with no credit card, or self-host it free
slides.note: The difference from Station 2: Vapi tools do one thing during the call. n8n can do many things in a row, branch on what the caller said, wait, and keep working after the call ends. Next slide shows what that looks like.

slides.title: What an n8n workflow looks like
bullets: A support hotline: the caller says their name and company
lookupCustomer: n8n finds them in HubSpot (industry, plan) and tells the agent who's calling
The agent talks to them like it knows them: "I see Northwind is on our Enterprise plan in healthcare"
createTicket: Claude writes up the bug, Asana creates the task and assigns an engineer, HubSpot notes it
The agent reads back the ticket number before they hang up
Later, a second workflow: when the engineer marks it done in Asana, Gmail emails the customer
slides.note: Walk the picture with the phone conversation on the right. Two tools, one n8n webhook: a Switch sends each tool to its own path, the same way n8n's own Vapi booking templates work. The phone part is still Vapi with Deepgram listening and speaking. HubSpot plus Asana plus an email when it's fixed is the part Vapi can't do alone. You won't build all of this tonight: the Station 3 steps start with one webhook.

slides.title: Just for fun: karaoke night
bullets: Guests call your agent to sign up for a song
The agent asks their name and what they want to sing
addSong: n8n searches YouTube for the karaoke version
Adds it to the "Karaoke night" playlist playing on your TV
Counts the queue, and the agent says "You're number 4. Watch the TV."
slides.note: The fun one. One tool, one webhook. The search step uses the HTTP Request node with the YouTube search API (the YouTube node has Playlist Item: Add but no plain search). Log in to n8n with the Google account that owns the playlist. Heads-up if anyone builds it for real: a TV that's already playing the playlist may need it reopened to show new songs.

slides.title: Start in Vapi, move to n8n
bullets: Yes, they work together. Your Vapi agent stays your agent.
During the call: a Vapi API Request tool calls your n8n Webhook (use the Production URL)
n8n does the work and answers with Respond to Webhook. The agent says the result.
After the call: point Vapi's server URL at an n8n Webhook to get the full call report
n8n can call people back through your Vapi agent (needs a Twilio number: free Vapi numbers only take calls)
So build in Vapi first, then move to n8n when you want more
slides.note: This answers the question everyone asks: do I have to pick one? No. Station 2 people can walk over to Station 3 later and keep the same agent. There's no official Vapi node in n8n; the webhook is how Vapi's own docs connect them.

slides.title: Ears, brain, mouth

Brain: Claude Haiku (fast, so no awkward pauses)

slides.title: The agent decides, the tool does
bullets: 1. The caller asks for something
2. The agent decides it needs a tool and fills in the details
3. Vapi runs the tool: your calendar, a sheet, Slack, n8n
4. The tool answers: worked or failed

slides.title: Vapi Composer: the cheat code

flow.title: The stations
flow.note: Pick your station. Every step has the exact clicks, and most have a screenshot.

sections.title: Station 1: your first phone agent in 20 minutes
sections.summary: Never built a phone agent? Start here, headphones on, at your own pace. Write your own short prompt, or take the Flux interview if you'd like a more thorough one (it takes longer). Ears, brain, mouth: Flux listens, Claude Haiku thinks, Flux speaks.

steps.title: Get your Deepgram API key
steps.instruction: Open console.deepgram.com and sign up (no credit card; new accounts get $200 of free credit). In the left sidebar, under Manage, click API keys, then the pink Create a new API key button. Name it phone-tools, keep the default permissions, and create it. Copy the key straight away: it is shown only once. Keep it somewhere private, never in a chat, doc or screenshot.
steps.check: The key is saved somewhere private.

image.alt: Deepgram console API keys page with API keys in the sidebar and the Create a new API key button

steps.title: Give the key to Vapi
steps.instruction: Sign up at vapi.ai and open dashboard.vapi.ai. In the left sidebar, click Integrations (hover over the icons to see their names). Under Voice Providers, click the Deepgram card, paste your key and save. Tip: the search box at the top finds any provider.
steps.check: Deepgram moves up to the Connected row.

image.alt: Vapi Integrations page: Deepgram under Connected and under Voice Providers

steps.title: Create an assistant
steps.instruction: In the sidebar, click Assistants, then the green Create Assistant button. It makes one straight away with Vapi's default settings, so next you swap the three cards on its page: Transcriber (the ears), Model (the brain) and Voice (the mouth). Each card has a pencil icon in its corner.
steps.check: You are on your new assistant’s page and can see the three cards.

image.alt: Vapi Assistants panel with the green Create Assistant button

steps.title: Ears: Deepgram Flux
steps.instruction: Click the pencil on the Transcriber card. Click the Model box, type flux, and pick Flux General English. Flux knows when you have finished talking, so your agent stops cutting people off. Close the panel with the X.
steps.check: The Transcriber card says Flux General English, Deepgram.

image.alt: Vapi Transcriber Settings: searching flux shows Flux General English and Flux General Multilingual

steps.title: Brain: Claude Haiku
steps.instruction: Click the pencil on the Model card. Click the Model box, type haiku, and pick Claude Haiku 4.5 with the orange Anthropic logo. It is the fastest on the list: watch the Latency number at the top drop.
steps.check: The Model card says Claude Haiku 4.5, Anthropic.

image.alt: Vapi Model Settings: searching haiku shows Claude Haiku 4.5 and 5.5

steps.title: Mouth: a Deepgram Flux voice
steps.instruction: Click the pencil on the Voice card. Click the Voice model box, type flux, and pick Flux (Deepgram). Then open the Voice box under it, preview two or three voices and choose one that fits your agent.
steps.check: The Voice card shows a Deepgram Flux voice you like.

image.alt: Vapi Voice Settings: searching flux in Voice model shows Deepgram Flux

steps.title: Write your prompt (or take the interview)
steps.instruction:
Two ways to get a prompt. Pick one.

Confident writing your own? Do it now and move on: it's the quick way.

Want a more thorough, planned prompt? Take the Flux interview: a voice agent asks about your business and writes the prompt for you. It takes longer, about 10 to 15 minutes. Open it here: https://dgeventhub.com/lessons/vapi-partner-event#run Paste the same Deepgram key there, answer its questions, then copy the prompt it writes into Vapi's System prompt box and come back to the next step.

Writing your own: The big System prompt box is under the three cards. Write who it is, its one job, what to ask for and how to talk. A template:
```
You are [name], the phone assistant for [business].
Your one job: [take an order / book a visit / answer questions about ...].
Ask for: [name], [what they want], [when]. One question at a time.
Keep every reply to one or two short sentences. This is a phone call: no lists or links.
If you don't know something, say so and offer to take a message.
```
Scroll to the bottom for First message: one short sentence that ends in a question, like 'Tony’s Pizza, what can I get you?'. Stuck for an idea? Ask ChatGPT or Claude: 'Write a short phone agent prompt for…'. Then click the orange Publish button, top right.
steps.check: Your prompt is in and you pressed Publish.

image.alt: Vapi assistant page: System prompt box, First message at the bottom, Talk and Publish at the top right

steps.title: Talk to it in the browser
steps.instruction: Click Talk (top right, next to Publish), allow the microphone and talk to it with your headphones on. Cutting you off? Check the transcriber is Flux. Rambling? Add 'two sentences max' near the top of the prompt. Change one thing, Publish, Talk again.
steps.check: It answers you and stays on its job.

image.alt: Vapi assistant page with Flux, Claude Haiku 4.5 and Deepgram cards, and the Talk button at the top right

steps.title: Get a free phone number
steps.instruction: In the sidebar, click Phone Numbers, then Create Phone Number. The window opens on Import Twilio: click Free Vapi Number on the left instead. Type a US area code (415 is often sold out; try 707 or 628) and click Create. Free numbers are US only, one per account, and take incoming calls only. It can take a couple of minutes to go live.
steps.check: Your new number is in the list.

image.alt: Vapi Create Phone Number window with Free Vapi Number selected and the Area code box

steps.title: Point the number at your agent and call it
steps.instruction: Open your number and scroll down to Inbound Settings. Under Assistant, choose your assistant. If the top right button says Save, click it; when it says Saved, you're set. Call the number from your phone. Bam: you have a phone agent.
steps.check: It picks up when you call.

image.alt: Vapi phone number Inbound Settings with an assistant chosen

sections.title: Station 2: Vapi Composer and built-in tools
sections.summary: Already have a phone agent? Give it something to do. Composer is the cheat code: it builds and changes things in Vapi from plain English. No code.

steps.title: Open Composer on your agent
steps.instruction: Open your assistant’s page and click Composer (top right). It opens beside your agent and already knows which one you’re on. Leave the mode under the message box on Ask for approval, so you see every change before it happens. Not sure where to start? Click Improve this agent.
steps.check: Composer is open beside your assistant.

image.alt: Vapi Composer panel beside an assistant, with an example request typed in

steps.title: Ask it to improve things
steps.instruction:
Try a few of these, one at a time, and approve the changes you like:
```
Keep every answer to two sentences and sound friendlier.
If the caller goes quiet for 10 seconds, ask if they're still there, then end the call politely.
Add a tool that transfers the caller to my cell if they ask for a human.
Why does my agent keep interrupting people?
Generate a test suite for my agent.
```
Approve the changes you like, press Publish, then Talk to hear the difference.
steps.check: At least one change is published and you can hear it.

steps.title: Connect Google or Slack
steps.instruction: Built-in tools need a one-time connection. In the sidebar, click Integrations and type google or slack in the search box. Under Tool Providers, click Google Calendar, Google Sheets or Slack and connect your account. Use a test calendar or a new sheet, not your real one.
steps.check: The provider shows as connected.

image.alt: Vapi Integrations, Tool Providers with Google Calendar, Google Sheets and Slack

steps.title: Add a tool (or ask Composer to)
steps.instruction:
In the sidebar, click Tools, then Create Tool. Scroll the menu to Integrations and pick one:
• Google Calendar: it has two kinds, Check Availability and Create Event. Make one of each. Set the time zone (it defaults to UTC).
• Google Sheets: Add Row. Paste the sheet ID (the part of the sheet’s URL between /d/ and /edit). Put headers in row 1: name, request, phone, time.
• Slack: Send Message. Name the channel in the description, and invite the Vapi app to that channel.
Other handy ones in the same menu: Transfer Call, Hang Up, Send Text, Query (answers from your files).
Fill in the Description: it’s how the agent knows WHEN to use the tool. Or tell Composer: 'I want my agent to check my calendar before booking appointments.'
steps.check: The tool is saved.

image.alt: Vapi Tools, Create Tool menu listing tool types

steps.title: Attach it and add the golden rule
steps.instruction:
Open your assistant, click the Tools tab, then Add tool, and pick your tool. In the System Prompt, add when to use it and the golden rule:
```
Read the details back and get a yes before you use any tool.
Only say something is booked or sent after the tool says it worked.
If a tool fails, say so and offer to take a message.
```
Publish.
steps.check: The tool is listed on your assistant and you pressed Publish.

image.alt: Vapi assistant Tools tab with Add Tool

steps.title: Test it for real
steps.instruction: Talk to it, or call your number, and ask for the thing. Then check the calendar, sheet or Slack channel. Did it really happen? If not, open Logs, then Calls, and look at the tool call in the transcript.
steps.check: The event, row or message really appears.

steps.title: Extra credit
steps.instruction: Structured Outputs (on the same Tools tab, Add Field): pull out the caller’s name, request and mood after every call; results show in Logs. Query tool: upload a menu or FAQ and let the agent answer from it. Advanced tab: what it says when the caller goes quiet, and how long a call can last. Or ask Composer: 'What else could my agent do?'
steps.check: You tried one more feature.

sections.title: Station 3: workflows with n8n
sections.summary: For the more technical. Use n8n for the apps Vapi doesn’t have built in (Spotify, Notion, HubSpot, Shopify, Philips Hue, Discord and hundreds more), or to chain several apps in one call. Shape: Vapi API Request tool → n8n Webhook → your steps → Respond to Webhook → the agent says the answer.

steps.title: Get n8n
steps.instruction: Sign up at n8n.io for the free 14-day Cloud trial. No credit card needed. There’s no free Cloud plan after the 14 days (n8n’s free Community Edition is self-hosted only), so it’s perfect for tonight. Then create a new workflow.
steps.check: You have an empty workflow open.

steps.title: Start with a Webhook
steps.instruction: Add a Webhook node. HTTP Method: POST. Respond: Using 'Respond to Webhook' Node. Under Webhook URLs, click Production URL and copy it (not the Test URL: that one only works while you’re clicking Listen for test event).
steps.check: You have the Production URL copied.

image.alt: n8n Webhook node: Production URL, POST, path song-request, Respond using the Respond to Webhook node

steps.title: Add your steps
steps.instruction:
Pick a recipe. The caller’s details arrive in the webhook body (for example {{ $json.body.song }}). The example in the picture is Dana’s song line: Webhook → Spotify Search Song → Add an item to a playlist → Respond to Webhook.
• Song request (the demo): Spotify, Search → Spotify, Add an item to a playlist. Reply: 'Added <song> to the playlist.'
• Idea catcher: Notion, Create a database page with the caller’s name and idea. Reply: 'Saved your idea.'
• Lead to CRM: HubSpot, Create or update a contact → Discord, Send a message to your team. Reply: 'Got it, someone will follow up.'
• Order status: Shopify, Get an order by number. Reply with its status for the agent to read out.
Sign in to Spotify, Notion, HubSpot or Shopify inside each node when it asks (n8n calls this a credential).
steps.check: Each node runs green when you test it with sample data.

image.alt: An n8n workflow: Webhook, Spotify Search Song, Add an item to a playlist, Respond to Webhook

steps.title: Answer the agent
steps.instruction:
End with a Respond to Webhook node that returns JSON the agent can read out, for example:
```
{ "result": "Added {{ $('Search Song').item.json.name }} to the playlist" }
```
If something failed, return a status of failed and say why, so the agent never pretends. Set Respond With to JSON. Then click Publish, top right.
steps.check: The workflow says Published (top right).

image.alt: n8n Respond to Webhook node returning JSON with a result sentence built from the Spotify search

steps.title: Make the Vapi tool
steps.instruction: In Vapi: Tools, then Create Tool, then API Request (under Integrations). Tool Name: something like requestSong or bookVisit. Description: when to use it, for example 'Use after the caller confirms their name and request.' Don’t leave it empty: it’s how the agent knows when to call it. Request URL: your n8n Production URL. Method: POST. (Or ask Composer: 'Add a tool that sends the caller’s name and request to my n8n webhook URL.')
steps.check: The tool has a name, a description, your URL and POST.

image.alt: Vapi API Request tool: Tool Name, Description, Request URL and POST

steps.title: Say what the agent sends
steps.instruction: Scroll to Request Body and click Add Property for each thing the agent should fill in, like song and artist, or name, time and phone. Give each a short description. Save, then add the tool on your assistant’s Tools tab and Publish.
steps.check: The tool is attached to your assistant.

image.alt: Vapi API Request tool Request Body with song and artist properties

steps.title: Tell the agent when to use it
steps.instruction: Add to the System Prompt: when to call the tool, to read details back first, and the golden rule: only say it worked if the tool’s answer says it worked. Publish.
steps.check: The rules are in the prompt.

steps.title: Call it and watch it run
steps.instruction: Call your agent and ask for the thing. In n8n, open Executions to watch the run. In Vapi, Logs, then Calls shows what the agent sent. Check the playlist, Notion page, CRM or Discord channel.
steps.check: The phone call made something real happen.

steps.title: Show the room
steps.instruction: Call your agent on speaker, ask it to do its thing, then show the calendar, sheet or Slack message it made. Two minutes each.
steps.check: The room heard it work.

troubleshooting: Your number rings out: open the number in Vapi and check an assistant is chosen under Inbound Settings. New numbers can take a few minutes.
Vapi ignores your changes: you didn't press Publish.
No Flux voice in the Voice card: pick Deepgram Aura-2 instead.
The tool never fires: it isn't on the assistant's Tools tab, or the prompt and tool description never say when to use it.
Calendar books at the wrong time: set the time zone on the tool. It defaults to UTC.
Slack posts nothing: invite the Vapi app to the channel and name the channel in the tool description.
n8n never runs: you used the Test URL, or the workflow isn't active. Use the Production URL.
The agent says 'done' but nothing happened: add the golden rule to the prompt and return a clear status from the tool.
It talks over you: use headphones, and check the transcriber is Flux.
